section_title: If God can save, why does salvation seem so far away?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 1 Surely the arm of the LORD is not too short to save, nor His ear too dull to hear. 2 But your iniquities have built barriers between you and your God, and your sins have hidden His face from you, so that He does not hear. 3 For your hands are stained with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken lies, and your tongue mutters injustice. 4 No one calls for justice; no one pleads his case honestly. They rely on empty pleas; they tell lies; they conceive mischief and give birth to iniquity.

5 They hatch the eggs of vipers and weave a spider’s web. Whoever eats their eggs will die; crack one open, and a viper is hatched. 6 Their cobwebs cannot be made into clothing, and they cannot cover themselves with their works. Their deeds are sinful deeds, and acts of violence are in their hands. 7 Their feet run to evil; they are swift to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are sinful thoughts; ruin and destruction lie in their wake. 8 The way of peace they have not known, and there is no justice in their tracks. They have turned them into crooked paths; no one who treads on them will know peace.

9 Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us. We hope for light, but there is darkness; for brightness, but we walk in gloom. 10 Like the blind, we feel our way along the wall, groping like those without eyes. We stumble at midday as in the twilight; among the vigorous we are like the dead. 11 We all growl like bears and moan like doves. We hope for justice, but find none, for salvation, but it is far from us. 12 For our transgressions are multiplied before You, and our sins testify against us. Our transgressions are indeed with us, and we know our iniquities: 13 rebelling and denying the LORD, turning away from our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering lies from the heart.

14 So justice is turned away, and righteousness stands at a distance. For truth has stumbled in the public square, and honesty cannot enter. 15 Truth is missing, and whoever turns from evil becomes prey. The LORD looked and was displeased that there was no justice. 16 He saw that there was no man; He was amazed that there was no one to intercede. So His own arm brought salvation, and His own righteousness sustained Him. 17 He put on righteousness like a breastplate, and the helmet of salvation on His head; He put on garments of vengeance and wrapped Himself in a cloak of zeal.

context_lines: The Lord’s inability is ruled out at the start. His arm is not too short to save and His ear is not too dull to hear. The barrier is the people’s iniquity: bloodshed, lies, dishonest claims and injustice mark their dealings.
Vipers’ eggs and cobwebs picture the harm and futility of what they produce. Their plans bring violence without providing a covering. Their paths leave ruin behind them and do not lead to peace.

The voice changes to confession. The people describe groping in darkness, longing for justice and salvation without finding them. They acknowledge that their many sins testify against them: rebellion, denial of the Lord, oppression and lies from the heart.

The picture widens to a public life where truth has fallen and the person who leaves evil becomes prey. The Lord sees the absence of justice and of anyone able to intervene. His own arm brings salvation, and He puts on righteousness and salvation like armor, together with vengeance and zeal.
common_interpretation_lines: [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/isaiah/59.htm) and [Wesley](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/isaiah/59.htm) emphasize the damage sin does to the people’s relationship with God and to their life together. Their wrongdoing cannot supply the security they seek.

Both see a movement from exposed guilt and acknowledged misery to God’s own intervention. The failure of human justice does not leave Him without power or resolve to act. The armor picture describes the righteousness of His cause and His commitment to rescue and judgment.
god_plan_lines: [Romans 3:9–26](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/3.htm) uses the description of feet running to bloodshed and paths without peace as part of its account of human sin. Paul’s point includes both Jews and Greeks: everyone is accountable, and righteousness comes through faith in Jesus Christ rather than through works of the law.

[Ephesians 6:10–20](https://biblehub.com/bsb/ephesians/6.htm) takes up the breastplate of righteousness and helmet of salvation in its call to put on God’s armor. Believers are to stand in His strength, armed with truth, faith, His word and prayer.

The change of setting matters. Isaiah describes the Lord acting to rescue and judge; Ephesians calls His people to depend on what He supplies and says their struggle is against spiritual evil, rather than flesh and blood. God’s armor is not permission to carry out private vengeance.
